limitations: Public announcements do not conclusively establish financial condition.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: When OpenAI dies it will likely fold into Microsoft, sharply cut compute demand, likely end free ChatGPT and raise prices.

statement.excerpt: When OpenAI dies — likely folding into Microsoft in the process — it will massively pull back on any and all compute demands, with the likely end of and free ChatGPT and a massive price bump across the board.

from_speaker: likely end of and free ChatGPT
a massive price bump across the board
our_interpretation: Read 'dies' as business failure that ends OpenAI's independent operation or forces a distressed transfer of its core business. Ordinary restructuring does not suffice.
The firm, checkable core is a large and broad reduction in compute demand following that failure, including demand carried on by a successor.
Compare actual compute use or contracted usable capacity on a consistent basis before and after failure. Spending alone may change because prices change.
Treat absorption into Microsoft and the end of free ChatGPT as explicitly hedged adjuncts, not guaranteed outcomes.
Read the apparent typo about free ChatGPT as predicting the likely end of the free tier. Any price comparison must use comparable services.
No numerical threshold or deadline is stated. Do not impose the nearby speculative 2027 reference as a firm deadline.
criteria.support_condition: A qualifying failure occurs, followed by an unmistakably large, broad reduction in OpenAI's and its successor's compute demand. Record whether the hedged Microsoft, free-tier, and pricing developments also occur without treating them as certain commitments.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A qualifying failure occurs and a completed transition establishes that comparable compute demand is maintained or expanded across the continuing business, contradicting the predicted broad contraction.
